M-VAVE FM-1 / X0X EXTENDED EDITION

Every control.
One reference.

Find a sound, a channel, a CC or a feature. See its values, targeting rules and readback in the same place.

Built on X0X by Charles Vestal and contributors, itself a fork of Felucca by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments). Acultur8 adds the Extended Edition changes. Original project & full credits.

Prepared for the 0.1.30-calbeta candidate · 26 October 2026 UTC. Source and local replay checks pass;physical USB CC filtering/readback checks are bounded. Advanced remote-action hardware acceptance remains open. Reason external-clock clip/grid stability is unresolved. Averaging and fine-tempo controls are deferred and absent from this build. Browser-only entries require the separate compatible browser companion.

CONNECTION & ENCODING

Channels carry independent address spaces.

Fixed control channels

The same CC number can address different parameters on different channels. FM1 uses a fixed custom control map, independent of each part’s configurable note channel. Use the chart’s exact channel/CC pair; GM instrument CC conventions do not describe this map.

Each channel has 88 eligible ordinary addresses: CC0–31 and64–119. CC32–63 are reserved fine companions; paired14-bit CC is not implemented. CC120–127 are reserved channel-mode numbers, outside this custom map. Unassigned addresses do not acquire a meaning automatically.

A CC message is [0xB0 + channel − 1, CC, raw], with raw0–127. Immutable parameter number = (channel−1)×88 + (CC<32 ? CC : CC−32). This parameter number is used by exact transactions.

Raw is different from canonical

Most controls use round(raw × maximum /127). Use Inspect wire values for the actual conversion. Frequency cutoffs use a logarithmic table; sparse enums, lengths, release time and older follow/duration controls have special conversions.

Wide ranges cannot represent every value through CC7. The ordinary-CC exact transaction carries a canonical integer in three7-bit chunks. Optional paired14-bit precision and NRPN are not required for this exact path.

Lengths, tempo and transpose can use encoded values: a length pot0–63 means1–64 steps; tempo adds20 BPM; transpose subtracts24 semitones. Per-control details distinguish these.

Browse all 16 channel address spaces

Select a channel to inspect its occupied addresses. Grey cells are unassigned; diagonal cells are reserved. Each occupied cell opens the matching control.

AssignedUnassignedReserved

STRUCTURED EDITING

Choose the target before the value.

Pattern, part, bass, drum, strip, step, block and motion contexts belong to the input source: USB0, TRS1 or browser2. They do not follow the visible panel. Stage the needed selectors, then send selector.commit=1. Changing a selector invalidates the ready context and incomplete exact transaction. Re-establish context after source replacement or reset.

Selector address reference
SelectorChannel / CCCanonical range
selector.pattern12 / 74[0, 31]
selector.part12 / 75[0, 4]
selector.drum12 / 76[0, 10]
selector.bass12 / 77[0, 1]
selector.step12 / 78[0, 63]
selector.block_low12 / 79[0, 127]
selector.block_high12 / 80[0, 1]
selector.motion_low12 / 81[0, 127]
selector.motion_high12 / 82[0, 1]
selector.kit13 / 12[0, 1]
selector.strip13 / 13[0, 24]
selector.seed_byte13 / 14[0, 3]
selector.commit13 / 15[0, 1]
selector.parameter_low13 / 16[0, 127]
selector.parameter_high13 / 17[0, 15]
selector.destination_pattern13 / 108[0, 31]

Pattern0..31 = P1..P32; part0=909,1=808,2=303A,3=303B,4=BREAK; kit0=909,1=808; bass0=A,1=B; strip0..10=909,11..21=808,22=A,23=B,24=BREAK. Step selector0..63 differs from the new one-based single-NOTE selector. Block = low +128×high (0..191); motion lane = low +128×high (0..159). Invalid combined contexts reject.

Exact canonical-value transaction
  1. Commit an explicit valid context.
  2. Set selector.parameter_low to parameter &127 and selector.parameter_high to parameter >>7. The high selector itself scales0..15, so its raw value may differ.
  3. Set value.exact_low7, value.exact_mid7 and value.exact_high7 to the canonical value’s three little-endian7-bit chunks.
  4. Send value.exact_commit=1. All three chunks and a ready context are required.

The old high2 field remains a16-bit compatibility path. Framing cannot target itself, selectors, or the new remote request/arm/cancel framing. Valid-range membership, project ownership, protection and feature guards still apply.

Example: parameter1227 (seed byte0), canonical120: parameter low75; parameter high9 uses raw76; value chunks120,0,0; commit raw127. The planner download uses this exact path for every recipe field.

Actions, history and persistence

Action buttons use low then rising nonzero, not a stream of repeated high values. Clear/copy/reset and song edits require a matching legacy arm code and stopped preflight. COPY requires an explicit committed destination. Undo/Redo use shared stopped project history. Confirmation, recording, busy queues and protected storage can reject a request.

Remote 303 arm and legacy destructive-action arm share guard storage. Read the matching 303 result before unrelated legacy arming. No automatic CC echo is provided. A sent message or accepted arm alone is not evidence of a musical edit or saved state.

303 AUTOMATION · SINCE 0.1.22

Generate a line. Change one note.

Both 303s support deterministic whole-line generation and pitch randomization of one existing active NOTE. Choose mode, chord block, KEEP/length, ALL/step and all four seed bytes, then a new monotonically increasing14-bit request ID. A nonzero32-bit seed is required.

  1. Commit consistent pattern, part, bass and strip: part2/bass0/strip22 for303A; part3/bass1/strip23 for303B.
  2. Stage the recipe and request ID. Read back context/recipe if needed.
  3. With transport stopped and the engine queue drained, send arm code2 (raw36), then execute low0/high127.
  4. Read command51 page4. Require a valid receipt with the same request ID, state APPLIED or NO_CHANGE and reason OK. Independently read command49 to confirm actual musical data.

Single NOTE changes only pitch, preserving flags, length, seed and other project bytes. REST, TIE and inactive targets refuse; no legal alternative returns NO_CHANGE. Whole-line generation uses normal generation semantics. Cancellation disarms unexecuted work; it does not Undo completed edits.

Use a copied pattern or an explicitly approved target. Recipe/context changes after arming invalidate it. Repeating a completed request with identical untouched context/recipe never generates twice; reused IDs with changed payload refuse. Query after a timeout instead of replaying blindly. Establish a fresh source session at request wrap/reset.

DRUM AUTOMATION · SINCE 0.1.23

Generate a drum rhythm directly.

All22 drum lanes:909 and808. Explicitly select pattern,part/kit,drum and matching strip. Stage density,positions,anchor rules,seed index and KEEP/length;use a new request ID,arm3,then drum execute low/high. Only the selected hit row and optional length change. Sounds,accents,motion,swing and other lanes are preserved.

CH14 CC94 density0–100;CC95 positions0 ALL/1 EVEN/2 ODD/3 OFFBEAT;CC96 anchors0 NONE/1 BEAT/2 BACK/3 KEEP/4 BEAT LOCK/5 BACK LOCK;CC97 seed index0–255;CC98 execute. Shared CC111 length0 KEEP or1–64. Exact transactions reach every seed index. Effective seed=index+1.

One source has one active generation family. A drum-specific setter replaces the303 recipe;stage shared length afterward. Family switching invalidates the arm and seed validity. Arm3 applies only to drums;arm2 still applies to303s. Legacy formats refuse changed drum length until independent lane storage is initialized. Position/anchor conflicts refuse unchanged.

Read command51 page3 for the staged drum recipe,page4 for the matching request result,and command49 for actual rhythm/length. Inspect drum controls.

GLO / MIDI

Isolate CC problems.

CC MODE:FULL / SIMPLE / OFF is a native GLO setting. FULL enables the map. SIMPLE allows fixed direct sound and sound-strip controls while blocking selectors,exact framing,generation,history,storage,CC transport and remote MASTER gain. OFF blocks all custom CC changes.

Notes/Note-Off,MIDI clock/Start/Stop and readback stay available. Switching mode invalidates queued CC,source contexts and arms;re-establish context before resuming FULL. Current project and gain are retained. Mode is session-only and returns FULL on init/project-load/reboot. There is no remote CC that can re-enable it.

Command51 page7 reports mode,active recipe family (0=303,1=drum,2=variation,3=Freeze/Commit,4=scoped copy) and aggregate accepted/rejected/unsupported/busy/coalesced/overflow counters. Queries do not clear counters or write settings. The compatible browser companion also blocks route-tagged slice CCs outside FULL.

VARIATION AUTOMATION · SINCE 0.1.24

Automate repeating variation.

Target any22 drum lanes or303 A/B with explicit pattern and matching part/kit/drum or bass/strip selectors. Stage cadence every2/4/8 passes,maximum0–8 changes,beat/back locks,seed0–255,mode,shape and region. For303s choose GEN,KEY,CHORD or BOTH constraints and an explicit chord block. No live chord capture;auto-mutate and missing/empty legal-note sets refuse.

Use a fresh shared request ID,arm4,then ON low0/high1. Arm5 plus OFF low0/high1 stops a matching live lane/pattern;both require stopped/drained transport. This is one global live recipe;source staging is private. A later source replacement invalidates older arms. Base pattern,Undo and saved project stay unchanged. Project revision alone cannot confirm a runtime-only change.

CH14 CC99–107 covers cadence,amount,locks,seed,mode,shape,region,ON and OFF;CH15 CC3/4 covers303 constraint and chord block. Exact framing reaches every seed/block. Drums:TOGGL/ADD/DROP;303s:NEAR/UP/DOWN. Shape:SAME/EVOLV;region:ALL/LAST4/LAST8/LAST16.

Read command51 page8 for staging,page4 for matching result and page9 for the actual live recipe. Readback remains available in SIMPLE/OFF;writes require FULL. Freeze/Commit controls and captured-step readback are described below. Download a plan-only wire example · Inspect variation controls.

SINCE 0.1.25

Capture a pass. Commit its notes.

Freeze any22 drum lanes or either303 through the same explicit matching variation/playback target. Use a fresh request ID,arm6,then Freeze low0/high1. Freeze may run during playback. Its receipt is PENDING until a complete accepted pass becomes HELD;303 requires forward direction and no first TIE. Base pattern,Undo and saved project remain unchanged.

Read command51 page5,index0. Require complete,gate validity and captured303 note validity. Read every active page6 step,then page5 again. Require identical capture ID and all five stamps plus unchanged header;retry at most3 times. Partial captured notes are unavailable. Capture ID is a content fingerprint,not a monotonic session ID. Accepted gates and final303 pitches describe engine state;physical MIDI/audio delivery remains a separate check.

Stop/drain transport. Stage a different destination0–31 and all four expected capture-ID bytes. Use a fresh request ID,arm7,then Commit low0/high1. Changed token,project,transport epoch,owner or destination refuses. Commit writes only that destination lane through the existing native transaction,with Undo/Redo. Destination accents,swing,sounds,other lanes/motion and source remain preserved. Only its destination probability lane is removed because accepted gates are baked in. Legacy shared drum destinations must already match captured length/rate. Save follows the existing autosave/manual policy;the MIDI plan does not send SAVE.

CH14 CC108 destination,CC109 Freeze,CC110 Commit;CH15 CC5–8 expected captured-token bytes0–3,little endian. Use exact framing for all token bytes. Read page4 matching result and command49 actual destination independently. Source reset,Cancel or mode changes withdraw pending remote Freeze;an already held pass is retained. Runtime capture resets on load/reboot;committed notes persist.

Download a plan-only Freeze wire example · Inspect Freeze/Commit controls. These custom controls require FULL;captured readback remains available in SIMPLE/OFF.

NEW IN 0.1.30-calbeta

Preview a scoped copy. Execute the checked request.

Use human CH15 CC9 source slot,CC10 destination slot,CC11 source scope,CC12 destination scope,CC13 preview/arm,CC14 execute. All slots are zero-based0–31. Scope0=ALL;1–11=909 BD,SD,LT,MT,HT,RS,CP,CH,OH,CR,RD;12–22=808 BD,SD,LT,MT,HT,RS,CP,CB,CY,OH,CH;23=303 A;24=303 B.

ALL must pair with ALL;any drum scope can copy to any drum scope;either303 can copy to either303. Same-pattern cross-part copy is supported. Identical source/destination tuples return NO_CHANGE. Stage all four targets and both shared request-ID bytes,then preview/arm1. Preview checks motion/Undo capacity without changing the project or its history. Read command51 page10 and require preview_valid1 plus page4 ACCEPTED for that request before sending execute0,then1. Project,transport,owner or recipe changes invalidate execution. Copies require FULL and stopped/drained transport.

Page10 returns source_pattern,destination_pattern,source_scope,destination_scope,recipe_valid_mask,preview_valid,current_fingerprint,referenced_bars,source_motion_count,destination_motion_count,same_target after the five common stamps. Scope and slot fields are staging readback;command49 independently reads actual notes,timing and motion. Referenced bars count distinct song bars using the destination scope;this is informational. Same_target compares the tuple,not all musical bytes. Capability,result and diagnostic readback respond in SIMPLE/OFF,where copy controls are blocked. Mode changes clear the source recipe;page10 then replies unavailable until restaged in FULL.

Destination swing and shared drum accents remain. Same-scope copies include scoped motion. Cross-part copies keep destination sound/tone automation and303 accents and generator accent setting;matching probability/conditions move with the notes. Legacy shared drum length/rate stay at the destination;initialized independent lane clocks follow the copied lane. Source and unrelated parts remain. One Undo transaction,Redo and explicit save/reload are tested;the plan sends no SAVE or transport action. Shared Cancel,shared arm0 or preview/arm0 disarm.

Download plan-only copy example:stored P2 snare to P3 mid tom · Inspect the six copy controls. Send only the preview prefix first and inspect readback before executing.

AUTOMATED VERIFICATION

Read the result. Verify the music.

Readback uses USB editor SysEx. Receiving controls over TRS does not provide a TRS output or reply path. The chart does not open MIDI ports or send messages.

CommandRead-only scopeRequest between F0 / F7 (hex)
48 /0x3025 project strip configurations; not DSP output.7D 46 4C 30 01 token strip
49 /0x31Unsaved musical pattern state. Section0 overview;1 lane0..24;2 motion0..159.7D 46 4C 31 01 token pattern section indexLow7 indexHigh7
50 /0x32Lane0..23 runtime snapshot: transport, queues, clocks, variation/capture/predicted masks. Prediction is distinct from accepted output.7D 46 4C 32 01 token lane
51 /0x33303/drum/variation/Freeze capability,source context,recipe,captured notes and latest result.7D 46 4C 33 01 token source page index
Command51 reply, pages, states and refusal reasons

Every successful page begins with five uint32 stamps: revision,queue_written,queue_read,transport_epoch,remote_generation. Payload values and CRC32 each use five little-endian7-bit chunks. CRC covers the bytes between F0 and the CRC. Match ABI, token, source, page and index before accepting a reply. CRC/length/field-count failures or unavailable pages fail the query; do not substitute a save/export or write.

Success: 7D 46 4C 33 01 token source page index status=0 field_count payload CRC. Refusal status1=invalid;3=unsupported/unavailable, with no field_count/payload. All inter-delimiter bytes are7-bit clean.

  • Page0 capability: cc_map1,query_abi1,feature_bits63 (bit0 303;bit1 drums;bit2 CC diagnostics;bit3 variation;bit4 Freeze/Commit;bit5 scoped copy),source_count3,firmware_identity9000126.
  • Page1 context: pattern,part,lane,context_ready,armed,staged_request,seed_mask.
  • Page2 recipe: mode,chord_block,length,note_step,seed32.
  • Page3 drum recipe: density,positions,anchors,seed_index,effective_seed,length,seed_valid. Available for active drum family;page2 is303-only.
  • Page7 diagnostics: cc_mode,recipe_kind,accepted,rejected,unsupported,busy,coalesced,overflow.
  • Page8 staged variation: every,amount,anchor_lock,seed,variation_mode,shape,range,constraint_mode,chord_block,seed_valid,off_request. Variation family only.
  • Page9 global live variation: lane255=OFF,pattern,every,amount,seed,locks,mode,shape,range,notes_mask,low/high_note,context_matches.
  • Page5 capture header,index0: capture_id,owner_lane,owner_pattern,state,length,rate,count,complete,note_data_valid,gate_data_valid,context_matches,destination,destination_valid,operation,expected_capture_id.
  • Page6 captured step,index0..63: capture_id,step_zero_based,note,gate,accent,slide,flags,valid. Only complete HELD steps below length are available.
  • Page10 copy preview,index0: four explicit targets,validity,preview guard,fingerprint,references,selected motion counts and same-target hint.
  • Page4 result: receipt_valid,result_request,staged_request,state,reason,before_revision,after_revision,before_fingerprint,recipe_changed.

Variation pages8/9,drum page3 and diagnostic page7 are implemented. Capture pages5/6 and Freeze/Commit are implemented. Scoped-copy controls and preview page10 are implemented in0.1.30-calbeta.

States:0 IDLE;1 ACCEPTED;2 PENDING (Freeze is waiting for a complete held pass);3 APPLIED;4 NO_CHANGE;5 REJECTED;6 UNSUPPORTED;7 CANCELLED.

Reasons:0 OK;1 context;2 stale context;3 stopped required;4 queue busy;5 protected;6 owner busy;7 invalid value;8 missing notes;9 unsupported NOTE or auto-mutate;10 Undo capacity;11 cancelled;12 capture incomplete;13 unsupported capture direction/layout;14 same or missing destination;15 copy motion or Undo capacity.

Before/after stamps describe a guarded transaction;variation changes runtime state and can retain project revision. They are evidence only for a matching APPLIED/NO_CHANGE receipt. The last result belongs to one source and request; it is not an event history. Command49 supplies independent actual musical state. Commands49/50 also validate CRC and correlated snapshot stamps; command48 uses its bounded strip reply without the newer CRC envelope.
